text: Pulwama is a town and notified area council in the Pulwama district of Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir, located in the disputed Kashmir region, approximately 25 kilometres (16 mi) south of Srinagar, the state's summer capital. It was historically known as Panwangam and later as Pulgam. Situated at coordinates 33.8830554°N, 74.9208705°E, Pulwama lies at an altitude of 1,500 to 2,000 meters above mean sea level. The city receives an average annual rainfall of 505.3mm, with a peak of 772.30 mm recorded in 1998; temperatures range from as high as 37 °C (99 °F) to as low as −12 °C (10 °F). About 70% of its population is engaged in agriculture, while the industrial sector is growing, with notable industries in cement production, wood products, and food processing. On 12 February 2021, the Jammu and Kashmir government approved the formation of a board to review objections, representations, and suggestions regarding the draft master plan for Greater Pulwama 2020–2040. Several Smart Town projects are underway, including a Smart Clock Tower, LED displays, new footpaths, parking lots, children parks, segregated household waste systems, central verges, high mast lights, and new tricolour LED installations. According to the 2011 Census of India, Pulwama had a population of 18,440, comprising 10,070 males and 8,370 females; children aged 6 and under numbered 3,167, accounting for 17.17% of the population. The female sex ratio is 831, below the state average of 889, and the child female sex ratio is 718, also below the state average of 862. The literacy rate in Pulwama is 91.18%, higher than the state average of 67.16%. The city is located in the Kashmir Valley, and most residents are ethnic Kashmiris. The majority of the population, 94.59%, are Muslims, with Hindus making up the second-largest religious group at 4.63%; other minorities include Sikhs (0.34%), Christians (0.17%), Buddhists (0.02%), and Jains (0.01%), while 0.24% of the population did not declare their religion.
